chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever is obliged to pay the ransom (fidyah) for game he caught while in the state of ihram, if he is a pilgrim (hajj), he slaughters his sacrificial animal (hady) which is obligatory upon him at Mina; and if he is a pilgrim of Umrah, he slaughters it in Mecca opposite the Ka'bah.

key_terms.فِدَاءُ: Ransom or compensation for a religious obligation or violation
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim slaughter the ransom animal if they hunt while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the geographical jurisdiction for expiation (kaffarah) in hunting, distinguishing between the pilgrim of Hajj (who sacrifices at Mina) and the pilgrim of Umrah (who sacrifices in Mecca opposite the Ka'bah). It reflects the juristic consensus that the location of the sacrifice is tied to the specific ritual context of the ihram, ensuring the expiation is performed in the sacred precincts associated with that particular pilgrimage type.
